name: Saint Augustine of Hippo
history: A brilliant North African teacher of rhetoric who searched for truth through philosophy and the Manichees, and was converted in Milan in 386 through the prayers of his mother, the preaching of Ambrose and the letters of Saint Paul. As bishop of Hippo he wrote the Confessions and The City of God, and is one of the greatest Doctors of the Church.
life: Augustine was born at Thagaste and studied at Carthage, where he took a partner, with whom he had a son, Adeodatus. He joined the Manichees for nine years. Teaching rhetoric at Rome and then Milan, he went to hear Ambrose preach and was slowly won by his reading of the Scriptures. In the summer of 386, in a garden in Milan, he heard a child’s voice chanting, take and read, opened Saint Paul’s letter to the Romans, and his resistance gave way. Ambrose baptised him at Easter 387. Returning to Africa, he lived in community with friends until the people of Hippo pressed him to be ordained priest in 391; he became their bishop a few years later. For over thirty years he preached, judged disputes, cared for the poor and wrote on grace, the Trinity and the Church. He died in 430 as the Vandals besieged Hippo.
prayerTo: Saint Augustine, you knew the restless heart and found its rest in God. Pray for all who search for meaning in the wrong places, and for me, that I may not delay any longer in loving God above all things. Help me to seek the truth humbly and to live it with charity. Amen.
penance: Read a few pages of the Confessions today, or the passage of Romans 13:11–14 that converted him, and make an honest examination of conscience.
meditation: You have made us for yourself, Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you. What are you restless for, and have you brought it to God?
prayer: Give heed to our humble prayers, almighty God, and through the intercession of blessed Augustine, Your Confessor and Bishop, kindly grant Your oft-given mercy to those upon whom You bestow great hope in Your forgiveness. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
